However, as underlined in the Explanatory Memorandum of the Law, most provisions of the Directive were already transposed into national law, in particular by the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Law no. 254/2004 regarding the execution of the punishments and the deprivation measures of freedom ordered by the judicial bodies during the criminal trial.

There were however, a number of provisions of the Directive that required the adaptation of national law, these being in particular provisions in the field of the minor's right to information, the right to individual evaluation and medical evaluation, the right to inform the parent or guardian of the minor. This is what Law no. 284/2020 proposed.

items.heading: Article 2

provisions.textEn:
Composition of the court


(1) The cases in which the defendant is a minor shall be judged according to the rules of competence customary by the judges, designated according to the law.

(2) The court composed according to the provisions of par. (1) it remains competent to judge according to the special procedural provisions regarding minors, even if in the meantime the defendant has reached the age of 18 years.


(3) The accused persons who committed the crime while he was a minor shall be tried in accordance with the procedure applicable in cases with juvenile offenders, if at the time of the notification of the court he was not 18 years old. The court may decide to apply the procedure for cases with juvenile offenders and persons who, at the time of acquiring the status of suspect, had not turned 18, when it considers it necessary taking into account all the circumstances of the case, including the degree of maturity and the degree of vulnerability of the data subject

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies until the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed a criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

provisions.textEn:
Composition of the court

(1) The cases in which the defendant is a minor shall be judged according to the rules of competence customary by the judges, designated according to the law.

(2) The court composed according to the provisions of par. (1) it remains competent to judge according to the special procedural provisions regarding minors, even if in the meantime the defendant has reached the age of 18 years.

(3) The offender who committed the crime during his / her minor period is judged according to the procedure applicable in the cases with minor offenders, if at the time of the notification of the court he was not 18 years old.

items.comment: See the comment above. The requirements of the Directive have no correspondent in national law if the accused turned 18 years old before the case went in court.

items.text: 4. This Directive applies to children who were not initially suspects or accused persons but become suspects or accused persons in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority.

provisions.textEn:
Informing about the status of suspect


Before the first hearing, the person who has acquired the status of suspect is informed of this quality, the fact for which the suspect, his legal classification, the procedural rights provided in Article 83, drafting a report (minute) in this regard.

Procedure in cases with minor offenders


General dispositions


The prosecution and trial of the crimes committed by minors, as well as the enforcement of the judgments regarding them are made according to the usual procedure, with the additions and exceptions provided in this chapter and in the section 8 of the chapter. I of Title V of the general part.

items.comment: If during questioning (usually as a witness), the minor becomes a suspect, the police or the public prosecutor must end the questioning and immediately inform the person about the consequences of his / her declarations. After this moment, once the status of suspect is acquired, all the rights (provided by Article 83 CCP) are granted. In this regard, the special procedure for minors for the CCP mentions that – as a common rule – all provisions from the CCP are applied as well, with some exceptions which are explicitly mentioned (nota bene!, in this later case, a more powerful standard of protection is granted, because of the age of the suspect).

items.text: 5. This Directive does not affect national rules determining the age of criminal responsibility.

provisions.textEn:
Regime of criminal liability of the minor



Limits of criminal liability


(1) The minor who has not attained the age of 14 years is not liable criminally. Related legislation

(2) The minor between the ages of 14 and 16 years shall be liable criminally only if it is proved that he committed the act with discernment.

(3) The minor who has reached the age of 16 years is criminally liable according to the law.

items.text: 6. Without prejudice to the right to a fair trial, in respect of minor offences:

provisions.textEn:
Consequences of criminal liability


(1) In relation to the minor who, at the date of the crime, was between the ages of 14 and 18, an educational measure not deprived of liberty shall be taken.

(2) With respect to the minor mentioned in par. (1) an educational measure deprived of liberty may be taken in the following cases:

a) if he has committed a crime, for which an educational measure has been applied which was executed or whose execution began before the crime for which he is tried;

b) when the punishment stipulated by the law for the crime committed is the imprisonment of 7 years or more or the life imprisonment.

items.comment:
In cases in which minors are criminally responsible, only education measures can be enforced. In this case it presents relevance the age at the moment when the offence was committed, not at the moment when the trial is taking place. Therefore, in all cases – before the investigative body or the court – and irrespective if the sanction imposed can not be privative of liberty (e.g., non-privative educational measures, the only sanction enforceable in case this is the first offence and the sanction provided by law does not exceed 7 years) all the general standards and rights apply.

The only scenario in which no educational measure will be enforced is regulated by Article 318 CCP, as procedural law institution – the so called waiver of prosecution solution. This can be decided by the public prosecutor in cases where the law stipulates the penalty of the fine or the punishment of imprisonment for a maximum of 7 years, and when there is no public interest in the prosecution. The solution of the prosecutor must be checked for both legality and opportunity by the preliminary chamber judge (see Article 318 para. 12 et seq., amended by Emergency Ordinance no. 18/2016, following decision no. 23/2016 of the Constitutional Court). Therefore, in front of the court (in this case the preliminary chamber judge), the general standards apply.

items.comment:
As already mentioned, in cases where suspect or accused person is deprived of liberty, irrespective of the stage of the criminal proceedings or the penalty provided by law, we are in the cases of compulsory legal assistance. Therefore, an ex officio lawyer will be appointed by the authorities, if the suspect or accused person does not hire a certain lawyer.


In addition, in Romanian law, all cases where the suspect or the accused is a minor are cases of mandatory legal assistance.


Therefore, in all proceedings the suspect or accused will be assisted or represented by a lawyer, with no exception. If he does not chose a lawyer, one will be appointed by the judicial organs ex officio, free of any charge.

In Romanian law, in cases where the suspect or the accused is a minor, legal assistance is always mandatory.

Request to reopen the criminal case


(1) The request for reopening of the criminal case may be made by the missing person and is addressed to the court that has tried the case in the first instance.

(2) When the person judged in default is deprived of liberty, the application may be submitted to the administration of the place of detention, which will send it immediately to the competent court.

(3) The request is made in writing and must be motivated with regard to the fulfillment of the conditions stipulated in Article 466.

(4) The application may be accompanied by copies of the documents from which the missing person understands to be used in the trial, certified for compliance with the original. When the documents are written in a foreign language, they will be accompanied by the translation.

(5) If the application does not fulfill the conditions stipulated in para. (3) and (4), the court envisages the person making the request to complete it by the first court term or, as the case may be, within a short term, set by the court.

Preliminary measures


(1) Upon receipt of the request to reopen the criminal case, a deadline for examining the admissibility is set in principle, the president having the attachment of the case file, as well as the summons of the main interested parties and procedural subjects.

(2) When the person who has requested the reopening of the criminal case is deprived of liberty, even in another case, the president shall order his knowledge about the term and take measures for the appointment of an ex-officio lawyer.

(3) The person deprived of liberty shall be brought to trial.

Judging the request to reopen the process


(1) The court, listening to the conclusions of the prosecutor, the parties and the main procedural subjects, examines whether:

a) the request was formulated in time and by a person from the ones provided in Article 466;

b) legal grounds for the reopening of the criminal case were invoked;

c) the reasons on which the application is formulated were not presented in a previous request for reopening the criminal case, which was definitively judged.

(2) The application shall be examined urgently, and if the convicted person is in the execution of the prison sentence applied in the case for which re-examination is requested, the court may suspend the reasons, in whole or in part, the execution of the decision and may order compliance with to the convicted of one of the obligations provided in Article 215 para. (1) and (2). If the execution of the prison sentence has not started, the court may order the convicted person to comply with one of the obligations provided in Article 215 para. (1) and (2).

(3) If the court finds the fulfillment of the conditions provided in para. (1), orders by concluding the admission of the request to reopen the criminal case.

(4) If the court finds that the conditions stipulated in Article 466, orders by sentence the rejection of the request to reopen the criminal case.

(5) The conclusion by which the request to reopen the criminal case is admitted may be challenged with the fund.

(6) The decision rejecting the request to reopen the criminal case is subject to the same appeal as the decision rendered in the absence of the convicted person.

(7) The admission of the request for reopening of the criminal trial entails the legal cancellation of the decision rendered in the absence of the convicted person.

(8) The court reopens the criminal proceedings by extension and with respect to the parties that have not made a request, being able to decide also on them, without being able to create a more difficult situation for them.

(9) With the admission of the request to reopen the criminal case, the court, ex officio or at the request of the prosecutor, may order the taking of one of the preventive measures provided for in Article. 202 para. (3) The prosecutor or, as the case may be, the executing court notifies the detained or arrested person that he has the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State of the European arrest warrant and to communicate with him, directly or through through the lawyer elected or appointed ex officio in Romania, under the conditions provided by the Romanian law and with the assurance of confidentiality.

(4) If the detained or arrested person shows that he understands to exercise this right, the prosecutor or the executing court shall inform the issuing authority of the European arrest warrant without delay. The information transmitted by the issuing authority, by any means which leaves a written trace, shall be communicated without delay to the requested person through the administration of the place of detention.

(5) The provisions of Article 91 para. (4) apply accordingly.

(6) The arrested person who does not understand or speak the Romanian language has the right to an interpreter, provided free of charge by the court.

Applicable law


The requests addressed to the Romanian authorities in the fields regulated by the present law are fulfilled according to the Romanian norms of criminal procedural law, unless otherwise provided by this law.

items.comment:
As a general principle, Law no. 302/2004 is being completed, whenever necessary by the general provisons of the CCP, except for the cases where otherwise is stipulated).


Therefore, regarding the rights provided by Articles 4, 5, 6 and 8, Articles 10 to 15 and Article 18 applied in the case Romania is the executing state, all general comments made above (and bellow for Article 18) are applicable. As it can be seen, due to the fact that a series of provisions from the Directive have not been tranposed ( (see the provisions of the draft project amending the CCP in this regard), the same conclusions can be drawn regarding the particular transposition of Article 17 from the Directive in the field of EAW proceedings.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that national law in relation to legal aid guarantees the effective exercise of the right to be assisted by a lawyer pursuant to Article 6.
items.heading: Article 18

provisions.textEn:
Mandatory legal assistance of the suspect or of the accused person


Legal assistance is mandatory:


a) when the suspect or the accused person is minor (...).

items.comment: When the suspect or accused is minor, there is always a case of mandatory legal assistance, according to the CCP.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings and children who are requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 19
items.comment:
Article 336 CCP regulates the challenge during the ongoing investigation.


When the case is already in front of a court (be it the judge for rights and liberties, preliminary chamber judge or a court which deals with the merits of the case), the judicial review is the contestation or the appeal (if reunited with the merits of the case).

items.heading: Article 20

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that staff of law enforcement authorities and of detention facilities who handle cases involving children, receive specific training to a level appropriate to their contact with children with regard to children's rights, appropriate questioning techniques, child psychology, and communication in a language adapted to the child.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: The annual reports of the National Administration of Penitentiaries have no information on this topic. However, there were several project in the last years organized under the Norway Grants agreements. For example, see the project „Strengthening the capacity of the penitentiary system in the area of human capital development at the level of prison staff” or “Strengthening the capacity of Bacău Penitentiary for Minors and Young Offenders to Comply with the International Instruments on Human Rights”.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Member States, and with due respect for the role of those responsible for the training of judges and prosecutors, Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that judges and prosecutors who deal with criminal proceedings involving children have specific competence in that field, effective access to specific training, or both.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
According to the National Institute for Magistrates' website, each year there are several training course organised as part of the continuos training for judges and prosecutors.


Ussualy in groups of about 20 participants, 2 experts (usually prosecutors / judges or members of the Academia) take on an intensive 2 days long course.


Among the courses organised during the last year (2019) there were several which could be included here, for example, special teqnicues of organising the course of the hearing in court when dealing with vulnerable persons. Still, we must mention that the agenda of this meetings is not public. We made institutional adresses to the National Institute of Magistrates in order to obtain relevant data, but we have no answer yet.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of specific training as referred to in paragraph 2 to lawyers who deal with criminal proceedings involving children.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
The raport for 2018-2019 of the National Bar Association underlined the lack of coherence for ''specific treatment including preliminary counseling for certain vulnerable groups'', including children.


From our information, special courses were organised in order to help the lawyers when assisting children, under EU grants.

The agenda of these programs is no longer available on the official website of the National Bar. We made official addreses to the INPPA (the National Institute for Lawyer Training), but we received no data at this stage.

items.text: 4. Through their public services or by funding child support organisations, Member States shall encourage initiatives enabling those providing children with support and restorative justice services to receive adequate training to a level appropriate to their contact with children and observe professional standards to ensure such services are provided in an impartial, respectful and professional manner.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)
